category: Advanced Training, Adaptation, and Model Surgery
definition: Training sequence models on gold-truth prefixes (teacher forcing) while inference conditions on the model's own possibly-wrong outputs, a train-test mismatch called exposure bias.
details: Training sequence models on gold-truth prefixes (teacher forcing) while inference conditions on the model's own possibly-wrong outputs, a train-test mismatch called exposure bias. One motivation for training on self-generated data via RL and preference optimization, which close this gap.

explainer.lead: Teacher forcing and exposure bias describe a train-test mismatch in sequence models: training on gold-truth prefixes but inferring from the model’s own possibly-wrong outputs. It matters because this mismatch can degrade generation quality and motivates training on self-generated data.

tiers.eli5: During practice, a student is always given the correct previous answer, but during the real test they must rely on their own previous answers—which can be wrong and throw them off.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers mitigate exposure bias with scheduled sampling, reinforcement learning, or preference optimization so the model sees its own outputs during training. A pitfall is that pure teacher forcing can leave the model brittle at inference time.
tiers.paperLevel: Teacher forcing trains sequence models on gold-truth prefixes, while inference conditions on the model’s own outputs, creating a train-test distribution mismatch called exposure bias. One motivation for training on self-generated data via RL and preference optimization is to close this gap.

explainer.example: A translation model trained only on correct previous words may falter when its first generated word is wrong at inference, because it never practiced recovering from errors.
